text: Which network centrality measure defines a node's importance recursively -- as high when its neighbors are also high-importance nodes -- analogous to Google's PageRank?
explanation: Eigenvector centrality defines a node's importance in terms of the importance of its neighbors, the same recursive principle underlying Google PageRank. Betweenness centrality instead measures how often a node lies on shortest paths between other node pairs (bottleneck-ness). Closeness centrality measures average distance to all other nodes, and degree centrality simply counts direct neighbors -- neither incorporates neighbor importance.
